fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar closed at 0.7235 against the US dollar on April 9, 2026, advancing 0.70% on the week — the loonie sits 1.69% below its level one month ago and 2.03% above its level one year ago1. The move developed as the Bank of Canada overnight rate held at 2.25% for a seventh consecutive meeting while the US federal funds rate sat at 3.64% per the February 2026 print, leaving a rate differential of 139 basis points in favour of the US dollar23. The euro advanced 1.34% on the week to 1.1696 against the US dollar amid the run of eurozone HICP data carried at +1.9% in the December 2025 print4. Sterling rose 1.5% to 1.3432 following the run of UK price releases5, while the yen firmed 0.25% to 159.09 against the US dollar amid Bank of Japan policy expectations, with the pair up 7.93% year-over-year6. If CAD/USD holds above 0.7200 amid the 139 basis point rate differential, the 428 projects tracked in mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction at a combined C$259.7 billion would continue to convert US-dollar commodity revenue at the current exchange rate through The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine7.

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada yield curve held its normal upward-sloping shape on April 9, 2026, with the 2-year to 10-year spread at 63 basis points — the spread sits 3 basis points wider than the 60 basis point gap recorded one year ago2. The curve developed as the Bank of Canada overnight rate held at 2.25% for a seventh consecutive meeting, while long-end demand reflected the rotation into duration following the softer US labour data from the February 2026 release23. The 2-year yield closed at 2.95%, up 33 basis points from 2.62% one year ago, while the 10-year yield closed at 3.58%, up 36 basis points from 3.22% one year ago2. The 30-year yield closed at 3.94%, up 41 basis points from 3.53% one year ago — the steepest year-over-year move across the six tenors carried in the Bank of Canada Valet feed since April 20252. The 5-year to 10-year spread sits at 40 basis points2. If the 10-year yield holds near 3.58% amid the seventh consecutive Bank of Canada hold, The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the 802 utilities projects tracked at C$507.7 billion and the 1,687 infrastructure projects tracked at C$179.0 billion to financing costs at the long end of the curve, while the 211 residential projects tracked at C$44.4 billion would retain exposure to the 2.95% 2-year benchmark7.
